chapter: Building the band in New York
title: The importance of tenor saxophones in the band
summary: Basie says the two tenors were key figures, not specially arranged for, and that he likes tenor players.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. How important was he in the --
He was very important.. I mean, you he had two great tenor players there with Lester, in rehearsal. Very important and very instrumental in being key notes, key figures for the band. Tenors.
Would things be arranged for them?

No, just this tune (inaudible) arranged on two numbers some things would be melody, where they were very outstanding in each one of them, moreso than anybody else in the band that would be in the tenors.

And I think everybody else would like tenor players (inaudible). Good, solid, good tenor players, I mean, you didn't have many good swing (inaudible), not as many as they got now, because there are a lot of good tenor players now and there are a lot of (inaudible) youngsters that playing a lot of horn nowadays.
